The Seattle Mariners have one internship open:[Intern, Minor League Development](https://www.teamworkonline.com/baseball-jobs/seattle-mariners/seattle-mariners/intern-minor-league-development-2191164) , a season-long role that starts by 1 March 2027 and runs until the end of the 2027 minor-league season at one of five affiliates (Tacoma, Arkansas, Everett, Inland Empire or Peoria). It pays $11.00 to $20.77 an hour, "based on the state minimum wage of the affiliate location." It requires only a high school diploma and prefers college coursework, but it prefers experience with video and baseball technology such as BATS, Trackman and Hawk-Eye. It was posted on 21 September 2026 with no closing date on the Mariners' posting. This isn't a summer internship, and we found no Mariners front-office internship posted. Here's the cycle in plain words: you apply in fall 2026, and you start by 1 March 2027, about five months later.

## What Is a Seattle Mariners Internship?


A Seattle Mariners internship, today, is the Intern, Minor League Development role. The intern runs day-to-day video and technology operations for one minor-league affiliate: capturing, tagging and uploading video in BATS, collecting bullpen and batting-practice data, running Trackman, Hawk-Eye, Edgertronic and Blast equipment, and helping prepare advance scouting reports before each series. Interns travel with the team for home and road games. The Mariners'[job opportunities page](https://www.mlb.com/mariners/team/job-opportunities) also lists T-Mobile Park event staff and retail jobs, which are seasonal jobs and not internships. This page is about the club, not the[MLB league-office program](https://www.extern.com/post/mlb-internship-guide) .


## When Do Seattle Mariners Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


The Mariners run one season-long intake on a short lead. This year's role was posted on 21 September 2026 for a start by 1 March 2027, about 5.3 months ahead. An archived capture of the Mariners' own Jobvite page, dated 23 September 2024, shows a Baseball Operations intern posting that wanted candidates to start by 1 March 2025 and work through mid-October 2025. That's two late-September postings in two cycles we can see, with a gap year we couldn't check, so treat late September 2027 as expected, not confirmed.

### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


The Mariners' own posting states no closing date, but the TeamWork copy of the same role shows an end date of 21 October 2026, exactly 30 days after posting. That looks like the board's default setting, not a deadline set by the club, though it means the TeamWork listing may drop off soon. A season-long role starting by 1 March also needs relocation to an affiliate, so the club has reason to move early. Apply this month on the Workday board, and don't rely on the TeamWork listing staying up.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


The Intern, Minor League Development posting sets these rules:


• **Education:** high school diploma required; college coursework preferred.


• **Experience, strongly preferred:** BATS video charting software, TruMedia, PitchBase, Portable Trackman, Hawk-Eye and Edgertronic cameras; MLB or NCAA baseball experience; video editing in tools such as Movavi or Adobe Premiere Pro.


• **Must:** correctly identify pitch types, and be willing to relocate to the assigned affiliate for all home and road games.


• **Availability:** start by 1 March 2027 and work through the end of the minor-league season.


• **Not stated:** academic credit, GPA, work authorization and weekly hours.


### Is This Open to College Students and Graduates?


Yes to both. The only education requirement is a high school diploma, and college coursework is preferred. But the role runs from 1 March to the end of the minor-league season, which overlaps a spring semester and a fall semester, so a full-time student needs to check with their school. The posting doesn't mention academic credit, so ask before you accept.


## What Skills Do the Seattle Mariners Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


The posting names a technology stack. **Video and charting:** BATS, TruMedia and PitchBase, plus video editing in Movavi or Adobe Premiere Pro. **Performance science equipment:** Portable and stadium Trackman, Hawk-Eye, Edgertronic and Blast. **Baseball judgment:** correctly identifying pitch types is a must. **Teamwork:** supporting the affiliate's Trackman intern and coaches, and troubleshooting technology on the road.

## What Is the Seattle Mariners Application and Interview Process Like?


The Mariners don't publish an interview format. Here's what the posting and past applicants show:


1. **Find the role.** Open the Mariners' Workday board, or the Internships tile on the club's job opportunities page.


2. **Apply online.** The TeamWork listing tells applicants to complete the follow-up application screen after clicking Apply Now. A former front-office intern on Reddit says walk-in résumés are unlikely to be considered.


3. **Show your tools.** Lead with BATS, Trackman, Hawk-Eye or video-editing work, and be ready to identify pitch types.


4. **Interview and offer.** Steps aren't published. One 2023 commenter described recorded video answers to five or six questions for a Mariners analyst role.


Plan your relocation before you accept: the role assigns you to an affiliate and travels with the club.

## How Do You Stand Out for a Mariners Internship?


Three moves. First, show tools, not just interest. The posting names BATS, Trackman, Hawk-Eye and video editing as strongly preferred, so put any hands-on use at the top of your résumé. Second, prove pitch-type identification, which is a must. Charting a college or amateur game and describing the process is direct evidence. Third, show you can relocate and travel for the season. The role goes to one of five affiliates, and reviewers will want to see that you can start by 1 March. The Mariners don't publish an applicant count or a conversion rate, so treat the internship as the goal and ask about baseball operations paths while you're there.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Seattle Mariners internship?


No. The Mariners' board lists no 2026 internship. What is open is Intern, Minor League Development, posted on 21 September 2026 for a start by 1 March 2027, running to the end of the 2027 minor-league season. The next cycle is expected around late September 2027.


### Is the Mariners internship a summer internship?


No. It's a season-long role. Interns must be available to start by 1 March 2027, and the end date is set by the end of the 2027 minor-league season. Interns travel with the affiliate for home and road games, so plan around your spring and fall semesters.


### How much do Mariners interns earn?


The posting lists $11.00 to $20.77 per hour for this seasonal role, based on the state minimum wage of the affiliate's location. The Mariners also list paid public transportation and merchandise discounts, subject to eligibility. Weekly hours aren't stated, and Workday lists the role as part time.


### Do I need to be in college to apply?


No. The posting requires a high school diploma and prefers college coursework. It strongly prefers experience with baseball technology such as BATS, Trackman and Hawk-Eye, and with video editing. You must correctly identify pitch types and be willing to relocate to the assigned affiliate.


### Where would I work as a Mariners intern?


At one of the Mariners' minor-league affiliates: Tacoma, Arkansas, Everett, Inland Empire or Peoria. You relocate to the assigned affiliate and travel with the club for road games. Front-office roles sit at T-Mobile Park in Seattle, but none is posted as an internship today.


### Is there a Mariners Baseball Operations or business internship?


Not posted today. An archived capture of the Mariners' own page from 23 September 2024 shows a Baseball Operations intern posting then, at $20.00 per hour. Check the Workday board in fall for a repeat, and treat Instagram claims of a 2027 posting as unconfirmed.


### Where do I apply for a Mariners internship?


On the Mariners' Workday board, which the Internships tile on the club's job opportunities page links to. The same role is on the Mariners' TeamWork Online page, where you finish a follow-up application screen after clicking Apply Now. Walk-in résumés are unlikely to be considered.


### Do Mariners interns get full-time offers?


The Mariners don't publish a conversion rate or class size. The posting is for a seasonal internship with no stated path to a full-time role. Ask about baseball operations or player development openings during your season, and keep checking the board for entry-level roles.


The Mariners' Minor League Development internship is open now and starts by 1 March. While you apply, a[remote Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) takes about 5 to 10 hours a week and gives you a finished data project to discuss in the interview.
